proposal.lay_description: Despite evidence that endophytes play a critical role in plant-microbe interactions they are poorly represented in genome databases. Leveraging our unique culture collection, we propose a genomic survey of the Xylariaceae, one of the largest and most diverse families of fungi made up of endophytic, pathogenic, and saprotrophic (including wood degrading) species. Our project will uncover the evolutionary history of plant-endophyte symbioses as well as characterize secondary metabolite (natural product) pathways and plant cell wall grading enzymes important for biofuel production in these fungi.
proposal.title: Comparative and population genomics of Xylariaceae: exploring the roles of endophytic fungi in lignocellulose degradation, nutrient cycling, and secondary metabolite production

Leveraging our unique culture collection, we propose a genomic survey of the Xylariaceae, one of the largest and most diverse families of fungi made up of endophytic, pathogenic, and saprotrophic (including wood degrading) species. Our project will uncover the evolutionary history of plant-endophyte symbioses as well as characterize secondary metabolite (natural product) pathways and plant cell wall grading enzymes important for biofuel production in these fungi.
proposal.title: Comparative and population genomics of Xylariaceae: exploring the roles of endophytic fungi in lignocellulose degradation, nutrient cycling, and secondary metabolite production

proposal.lay_description:
In a collaborative effort, JGI staff are working together with fungal mycologists from several institutions as well as Arizona Genomics Institute, AGI, to develop a curriculum to train undergraduate and graduate students in fungal biology. Fungi collected and cultured by students will be sent to AGI for DNA extraction then to JGI for sequencing, assembly and annotation. In addition to educating the next generation of scientists, this will provide fungal taxonomic breath to Mycocosm. 

The learning outcomes for students include fungal culturing, experimental design and data analysis. The workflow consists of students isolating fungal endophytes in the outdoor environment, assaying these fungi under different stressors, documenting fungal phenotypic responses, and preparing fungal endophyte tissue for genome sequencing. Students will culture and prepare tissue to ship to AGI where DNA extraction will take place. DNA will be shipped to the JGI for Illumina fragment library construction and sequencing. We are requesting 5Gbp-10Gbp per sample. Although the goal is to annotate draft genomes, field isolated samples might carry the genomes of the source host and possible symbionts/contaminants. Therefore, we will classify student samples as metagenomes and the sequencing data will be processed by IMG’s newly built EukCC Pipeline. Eukaryotic bins resulting from EukCC will be annotated and released in Mycocosm. Using the data generated by JGI, students will conduct bioinformatic analyses to compare fungi with different stress responses to explore how genes may be linked to phenotypic responses. 

The goals of this project are to 1) develop a publicly available start to finish curriculum for students which includes fungal isolation and wet-lab phenotyping through to sequencing and comparative genomic analysis that can be integrated as a module within fungal biology courses; 2) characterize fungal communities (starting with endophytes) using student-sourced large scale data, 3) produce data for linking genotype and phenotype (stress responses) in endophytic fungi; 4) improve the availability of MycoCosm genome annotations; and 5) scale this project to cover a wider range of institutions and fungal genomes. Endophytes are often rich in secondary metabolites. If successful, this project will also facilitate discovery and characterization of novel bioproducts. Upon successful completion of this pilot, Co-PIs intend to submit a full CSP to support future sequencing efforts associated with this project. We will also jointly pursue funding through DOE or another source to support teaching lab costs and growth at the JGI to better enable -omics training for the next generation of scientists.

proposal.lay_description: Genomes of important model and many industrially important fungi are still incomplete. The goal of this project is: (a) to finish and annotate the genomes of ~25 strains, and (b) to carry out functional analyses by novel CRISPR/Cas9 approaches. The next quantum leap in biology will come by integrating all levels of genome, transcriptome, proteome, and metabolome data for detailed cross-species comparisons. Completion of this CSP will have sweeping impact on data interpretation of current and completed genome-wide studies and will advance evolutionary and chromatin biology.

organisms.label: Genome

proposal.lay_description: Despite evidence that endophytes play a critical role in plant-microbe interactions they are poorly represented in genome databases. Leveraging our unique culture collection, we propose a genomic survey of the Xylariaceae, one of the largest and most diverse families of fungi made up of endophytic, pathogenic, and saprotrophic (including wood degrading) species. Our project will uncover the evolutionary history of plant-endophyte symbioses as well as characterize secondary metabolite (natural product) pathways and plant cell wall grading enzymes important for biofuel production in these fungi.
proposal.title: Comparative and population genomics of Xylariaceae: exploring the roles of endophytic fungi in lignocellulose degradation, nutrient cycling, and secondary metabolite production

Leveraging our unique culture collection, we propose a genomic survey of the Xylariaceae, one of the largest and most diverse families of fungi made up of endophytic, pathogenic, and saprotrophic (including wood degrading) species. Our project will uncover the evolutionary history of plant-endophyte symbioses as well as characterize secondary metabolite (natural product) pathways and plant cell wall grading enzymes important for biofuel production in these fungi.
proposal.title: Comparative and population genomics of Xylariaceae: exploring the roles of endophytic fungi in lignocellulose degradation, nutrient cycling, and secondary metabolite production

proposal.lay_description: Black Fungi spread in diverse extreme environments playing a crucial role by recycling organic matter, enabling nutrient uptake. They are also involved in biogeochemical processes, including rock transformations, bioweathering, mineral formation. The STRES project aims to dig into the genome diversity and metabolites  involved in stress response to: i) gain insights into the evolutionary processes allowing Black Fungi to successfully adapt to extremes; ii) clarify their role in the functioning and balance in extreme-ecosystems; iii) explore the role of melanin in energy processes.

proposal.lay_description: Black Fungi spread in diverse extreme environments playing a crucial role by recycling organic matter, enabling nutrient uptake. They are also involved in biogeochemical processes, including rock transformations, bioweathering, mineral formation. The STRES project aims to dig into the genome diversity and metabolites  involved in stress response to: i) gain insights into the evolutionary processes allowing Black Fungi to successfully adapt to extremes; ii) clarify their role in the functioning and balance in extreme-ecosystems; iii) explore the role of melanin in energy processes.

proposal.lay_description: Genomes of important model and many industrially important fungi are still incomplete. The goal of this project is: (a) to finish and annotate the genomes of ~25 strains, and (b) to carry out functional analyses by novel CRISPR/Cas9 approaches. The next quantum leap in biology will come by integrating all levels of genome, transcriptome, proteome, and metabolome data for detailed cross-species comparisons. Completion of this CSP will have sweeping impact on data interpretation of current and completed genome-wide studies and will advance evolutionary and chromatin biology.
proposal.title: The curse of being first meets the need to be complete: Finishing genomes to leverage additional information from completed and ongoing JGI CSPs

proposal.lay_description: Despite evidence that endophytes play a critical role in plant-microbe interactions they are poorly represented in genome databases. Leveraging our unique culture collection, we propose a genomic survey of the Xylariaceae, one of the largest and most diverse families of fungi made up of endophytic, pathogenic, and saprotrophic (including wood degrading) species. Our project will uncover the evolutionary history of plant-endophyte symbioses as well as characterize secondary metabolite (natural product) pathways and plant cell wall grading enzymes important for biofuel production in these fungi.
proposal.title: Comparative and population genomics of Xylariaceae: exploring the roles of endophytic fungi in lignocellulose degradation, nutrient cycling, and secondary metabolite production

proposal.lay_description: Genomes of important model and many industrially important fungi are still incomplete. The goal of this project is: (a) to finish and annotate the genomes of ~25 strains, and (b) to carry out functional analyses by novel CRISPR/Cas9 approaches. The next quantum leap in biology will come by integrating all levels of genome, transcriptome, proteome, and metabolome data for detailed cross-species comparisons. Completion of this CSP will have sweeping impact on data interpretation of current and completed genome-wide studies and will advance evolutionary and chromatin biology.
proposal.title: The curse of being first meets the need to be complete: Finishing genomes to leverage additional information from completed and ongoing JGI CSPs

proposal.lay_description: We propose to investigate the genetic bases of fungal thermophily, biomass-degradation, and fungal-bacterial interactions in Sordariales, an order of biomass-degrading fungi frequently encountered in compost and encompassing one of the few groups of thermophilic fungi. Our proposal fits into the DOE mission because it focuses on biological processes of industrial interest, it explores the functional diversity of organisms that are essential for carbon cycling in ecosystems and it involves species related to N. crassa and P. anserina, model fungi for studying plant cell wall deconstruction.

proposal.lay_description: Black Fungi spread in diverse extreme environments playing a crucial role by recycling organic matter, enabling nutrient uptake. They are also involved in biogeochemical processes, including rock transformations, bioweathering, mineral formation. The STRES project aims to dig into the genome diversity and metabolites  involved in stress response to: i) gain insights into the evolutionary processes allowing Black Fungi to successfully adapt to extremes; ii) clarify their role in the functioning and balance in extreme-ecosystems; iii) explore the role of melanin in energy processes.

proposal.lay_description: The fungal genus Fusarium is highly diverse, consisting more than 300 phylogenetically distinct species that, collectively, occur as mutualists and/or plant pathogens on virtually all crops, including bioenergy crops such as corn, poplar, sorghum, soybean, sugarcane, and switchgrass. In addition, many species exist as saprotrophs in soil and other extreme environments. Because of their associations with plants, Fusarium species (fusaria) can profoundly impact “bioenergy” production and global “carbon cycling”.
proposal.title: Genome dynamics, chromosomal rearrangements and potential functional impacts in Fusarium, a genus of endophytic, plant pathogenic and saprophytic fungi

proposal.lay_description: The fungal genus Fusarium is highly diverse, consisting more than 300 phylogenetically distinct species that, collectively, occur as mutualists and/or plant pathogens on virtually all crops, including bioenergy crops such as corn, poplar, sorghum, soybean, sugarcane, and switchgrass. In addition, many species exist as saprotrophs in soil and other extreme environments. Because of their associations with plants, Fusarium species (fusaria) can profoundly impact “bioenergy” production and global “carbon cycling”.
proposal.title: Genome dynamics, chromosomal rearrangements and potential functional impacts in Fusarium, a genus of endophytic, plant pathogenic and saprophytic fungi

organisms.label: Genome

proposal.lay_description: Genomes of important model and many industrially important fungi are still incomplete. The goal of this project is: (a) to finish and annotate the genomes of ~25 strains, and (b) to carry out functional analyses by novel CRISPR/Cas9 approaches. The next quantum leap in biology will come by integrating all levels of genome, transcriptome, proteome, and metabolome data for detailed cross-species comparisons. Completion of this CSP will have sweeping impact on data interpretation of current and completed genome-wide studies and will advance evolutionary and chromatin biology.
proposal.title: The curse of being first meets the need to be complete: Finishing genomes to leverage additional information from completed and ongoing JGI CSPs

organisms.label: Genome

proposal.lay_description: Despite the persistent presence of potentially harmful fungi and bacteria, America’s native prairies are healthy, thriving communities of perennial herbaceous plants. How do these communities maintain a balance with these microbes? Bacteria and fungi found in native prairie soil, are mutually antagonist and thus may keep each other in check. Each produces antibiotic compounds when competing for food in the soil. By studying these interactions, we may discover novel antibiotics or other compounds that may be suitable as pharmaceuticals or other industrially useful compounds.
proposal.title: Mechanisms of co-evolutionary adaptation of soil microbes.

proposal.lay_description: Genomes of important model and many industrially important fungi are still incomplete. The goal of this project is: (a) to finish and annotate the genomes of ~25 strains, and (b) to carry out functional analyses by novel CRISPR/Cas9 approaches. The next quantum leap in biology will come by integrating all levels of genome, transcriptome, proteome, and metabolome data for detailed cross-species comparisons. Completion of this CSP will have sweeping impact on data interpretation of current and completed genome-wide studies and will advance evolutionary and chromatin biology.
proposal.title: The curse of being first meets the need to be complete: Finishing genomes to leverage additional information from completed and ongoing JGI CSPs

proposal.lay_description: The fungal genus Fusarium is highly diverse, consisting more than 300 phylogenetically distinct species that, collectively, occur as mutualists and/or plant pathogens on virtually all crops, including bioenergy crops such as corn, poplar, sorghum, soybean, sugarcane, and switchgrass. In addition, many species exist as saprotrophs in soil and other extreme environments. Because of their associations with plants, Fusarium species (fusaria) can profoundly impact “bioenergy” production and global “carbon cycling”.
proposal.title: Genome dynamics, chromosomal rearrangements and potential functional impacts in Fusarium, a genus of endophytic, plant pathogenic and saprophytic fungi

proposal.lay_description: The fungal genus Fusarium is highly diverse, consisting more than 300 phylogenetically distinct species that, collectively, occur as mutualists and/or plant pathogens on virtually all crops, including bioenergy crops such as corn, poplar, sorghum, soybean, sugarcane, and switchgrass. In addition, many species exist as saprotrophs in soil and other extreme environments. Because of their associations with plants, Fusarium species (fusaria) can profoundly impact “bioenergy” production and global “carbon cycling”.
proposal.title: Genome dynamics, chromosomal rearrangements and potential functional impacts in Fusarium, a genus of endophytic, plant pathogenic and saprophytic fungi

organisms.label: Genome

proposal.lay_description: Genomes of important model and many industrially important fungi are still incomplete. The goal of this project is: (a) to finish and annotate the genomes of ~25 strains, and (b) to carry out functional analyses by novel CRISPR/Cas9 approaches. The next quantum leap in biology will come by integrating all levels of genome, transcriptome, proteome, and metabolome data for detailed cross-species comparisons. Completion of this CSP will have sweeping impact on data interpretation of current and completed genome-wide studies and will advance evolutionary and chromatin biology.
proposal.title: The curse of being first meets the need to be complete: Finishing genomes to leverage additional information from completed and ongoing JGI CSPs

organisms.label: Genome

proposal.lay_description: The species of yeasts that colonize floral nectar face two major challenges: high osmotic pressure caused by excessive carbon supply and strong resource competition caused by low nitrogen availability. This project is aimed at identifying the genes and pathways that enable nectar yeasts to grow in the carbon- and nitrogen-stressed environment. Nectar yeasts have presumably evolved strategies to scavenge nitrogen and continue biomass production under conditions where other microbes perish. Understanding the genomic basis of these strategies has the potential to facilitate redesigning of microbes for biofuel production and carbon storage.
proposal.title: Genomic basis of the ecological success of nectar yeasts in their carbon-stressed and nitrogen-limited environments

organisms.label: Genome

proposal.lay_description: Despite evidence that endophytes play a critical role in plant-microbe interactions they are poorly represented in genome databases. Leveraging our unique culture collection, we propose a genomic survey of the Xylariaceae, one of the largest and most diverse families of fungi made up of endophytic, pathogenic, and saprotrophic (including wood degrading) species. Our project will uncover the evolutionary history of plant-endophyte symbioses as well as characterize secondary metabolite (natural product) pathways and plant cell wall grading enzymes important for biofuel production in these fungi.
proposal.title: Comparative and population genomics of Xylariaceae: exploring the roles of endophytic fungi in lignocellulose degradation, nutrient cycling, and secondary metabolite production

Our project will uncover the evolutionary history of plant-endophyte symbioses as well as characterize secondary metabolite (natural product) pathways and plant cell wall grading enzymes important for biofuel production in these fungi.

proposal.lay_description: Some beneficial plant associated fungi house bacteria inside their cells which impact fungal and plant health. Recent studies show that some fungal endosymbionts manipulate reproduction of their hosts, and may influence plant ecosystems. This project focuses on endosymbionts and fungal reproduction, expanding knowledge on the complexities of microbiome interactions. These fungi are industrially important because they produce valuable lipid products. Our goal is to learn about optimal conditions for fungal health and apply that knowledge to increase crop health and produce alternative energies.

proposal.lay_description: The species of yeasts that colonize floral nectar face two major challenges: high osmotic pressure caused by excessive carbon supply and strong resource competition caused by low nitrogen availability. This project is aimed at identifying the genes and pathways that enable nectar yeasts to grow in the carbon- and nitrogen-stressed environment. Nectar yeasts have presumably evolved strategies to scavenge nitrogen and continue biomass production under conditions where other microbes perish. Understanding the genomic basis of these strategies has the potential to facilitate redesigning of microbes for biofuel production and carbon storage.
proposal.title: Genomic basis of the ecological success of nectar yeasts in their carbon-stressed and nitrogen-limited environments

proposal.lay_description: The species of yeasts that colonize floral nectar face two major challenges: high osmotic pressure caused by excessive carbon supply and strong resource competition caused by low nitrogen availability. This project is aimed at identifying the genes and pathways that enable nectar yeasts to grow in the carbon- and nitrogen-stressed environment. Nectar yeasts have presumably evolved strategies to scavenge nitrogen and continue biomass production under conditions where other microbes perish. Understanding the genomic basis of these strategies has the potential to facilitate redesigning of microbes for biofuel production and carbon storage.

proposal.lay_description: Some beneficial plant associated fungi house bacteria inside their cells which impact fungal and plant health. Recent studies show that some fungal endosymbionts manipulate reproduction of their hosts, and may influence plant ecosystems. This project focuses on endosymbionts and fungal reproduction, expanding knowledge on the complexities of microbiome interactions. These fungi are industrially important because they produce valuable lipid products. Our goal is to learn about optimal conditions for fungal health and apply that knowledge to increase crop health and produce alternative energies.

proposal.lay_description: DNA methylation is a fundamental epigenetic modification that plays a critical role in genome function in eukaryotes This proposal will study the function of N6-methyladenine (6mA) in early divergent fungi because it is more abundant than in other eukaryotes and seems to regulate gene expression. The function will be studied in the context of responses to developmental and environmental signals, with special emphasis in those signals regulating lipid accumulation because of its relevancy for the production of biofuels.

proposal.lay_description: Despite evidence that endophytes play a critical role in plant-microbe interactions they are poorly represented in genome databases. Leveraging our unique culture collection, we propose a genomic survey of the Xylariaceae, one of the largest and most diverse families of fungi made up of endophytic, pathogenic, and saprotrophic (including wood degrading) species. Our project will uncover the evolutionary history of plant-endophyte symbioses as well as characterize secondary metabolite (natural product) pathways and plant cell wall grading enzymes important for biofuel production in these fungi.

proposal.lay_description: Genomes of important model and many industrially important fungi are still incomplete. The goal of this project is: (a) to finish and annotate the genomes of ~25 strains, and (b) to carry out functional analyses by novel CRISPR/Cas9 approaches. The next quantum leap in biology will come by integrating all levels of genome, transcriptome, proteome, and metabolome data for detailed cross-species comparisons. Completion of this CSP will have sweeping impact on data interpretation of current and completed genome-wide studies and will advance evolutionary and chromatin biology.
proposal.title: The curse of being first meets the need to be complete: Finishing genomes to leverage additional information from completed and ongoing JGI CSPs

proposal.lay_description:
In a collaborative effort, JGI staff are working together with fungal mycologists from several institutions as well as Arizona Genomics Institute, AGI, to develop a curriculum to train undergraduate and graduate students in fungal biology. Fungi collected and cultured by students will be sent to AGI for DNA extraction then to JGI for sequencing, assembly and annotation. In addition to educating the next generation of scientists, this will provide fungal taxonomic breath to Mycocosm. 

The learning outcomes for students include fungal culturing, experimental design and data analysis. The workflow consists of students isolating fungal endophytes in the outdoor environment, assaying these fungi under different stressors, documenting fungal phenotypic responses, and preparing fungal endophyte tissue for genome sequencing. Students will culture and prepare tissue to ship to AGI where DNA extraction will take place. DNA will be shipped to the JGI for Illumina fragment library construction and sequencing. We are requesting 5Gbp-10Gbp per sample. Although the goal is to annotate draft genomes, field isolated samples might carry the genomes of the source host and possible symbionts/contaminants. Therefore, we will classify student samples as metagenomes and the sequencing data will be processed by IMG’s newly built EukCC Pipeline. Eukaryotic bins resulting from EukCC will be annotated and released in Mycocosm. Using the data generated by JGI, students will conduct bioinformatic analyses to compare fungi with different stress responses to explore how genes may be linked to phenotypic responses. 

The goals of this project are to 1) develop a publicly available start to finish curriculum for students which includes fungal isolation and wet-lab phenotyping through to sequencing and comparative genomic analysis that can be integrated as a module within fungal biology courses; 2) characterize fungal communities (starting with endophytes) using student-sourced large scale data, 3) produce data for linking genotype and phenotype (stress responses) in endophytic fungi; 4) improve the availability of MycoCosm genome annotations; and 5) scale this project to cover a wider range of institutions and fungal genomes. Endophytes are often rich in secondary metabolites. If successful, this project will also facilitate discovery and characterization of novel bioproducts. Upon successful completion of this pilot, Co-PIs intend to submit a full CSP to support future sequencing efforts associated with this project. We will also jointly pursue funding through DOE or another source to support teaching lab costs and growth at the JGI to better enable -omics training for the next generation of scientists.

organisms.label: Genome

proposal.lay_description: Genomes of important model and many industrially important fungi are still incomplete. The goal of this project is: (a) to finish and annotate the genomes of ~25 strains, and (b) to carry out functional analyses by novel CRISPR/Cas9 approaches. The next quantum leap in biology will come by integrating all levels of genome, transcriptome, proteome, and metabolome data for detailed cross-species comparisons. Completion of this CSP will have sweeping impact on data interpretation of current and completed genome-wide studies and will advance evolutionary and chromatin biology.
proposal.title: The curse of being first meets the need to be complete: Finishing genomes to leverage additional information from completed and ongoing JGI CSPs

proposal.lay_description: We propose to investigate the genetic bases of fungal thermophily, biomass-degradation, and fungal-bacterial interactions in Sordariales, an order of biomass-degrading fungi frequently encountered in compost and encompassing one of the few groups of thermophilic fungi. Our proposal fits into the DOE mission because it focuses on biological processes of industrial interest, it explores the functional diversity of organisms that are essential for carbon cycling in ecosystems and it involves species related to N. crassa and P. anserina, model fungi for studying plant cell wall deconstruction.

proposal.lay_description: DNA methylation is a fundamental epigenetic modification that plays a critical role in genome function in eukaryotes This proposal will study the function of N6-methyladenine (6mA) in early divergent fungi because it is more abundant than in other eukaryotes and seems to regulate gene expression. The function will be studied in the context of responses to developmental and environmental signals, with special emphasis in those signals regulating lipid accumulation because of its relevancy for the production of biofuels.
proposal.title: Exploring the role of DNA methylation in biofuel production, environmental sensing and development in basal fungi

proposal.lay_description: Despite evidence that endophytes play a critical role in plant-microbe interactions they are poorly represented in genome databases. Leveraging our unique culture collection, we propose a genomic survey of the Xylariaceae, one of the largest and most diverse families of fungi made up of endophytic, pathogenic, and saprotrophic (including wood degrading) species. Our project will uncover the evolutionary history of plant-endophyte symbioses as well as characterize secondary metabolite (natural product) pathways and plant cell wall grading enzymes important for biofuel production in these fungi.
proposal.title: Comparative and population genomics of Xylariaceae: exploring the roles of endophytic fungi in lignocellulose degradation, nutrient cycling, and secondary metabolite production

proposal.lay_description: We propose to investigate the genetic bases of fungal thermophily, biomass-degradation, and fungal-bacterial interactions in Sordariales, an order of biomass-degrading fungi frequently encountered in compost and encompassing one of the few groups of thermophilic fungi. Our proposal fits into the DOE mission because it focuses on biological processes of industrial interest, it explores the functional diversity of organisms that are essential for carbon cycling in ecosystems and it involves species related to N. crassa and P. anserina, model fungi for studying plant cell wall deconstruction.
proposal.title: Comparative genomics and association mapping in Sordariales: insights into functional diversity in Neurospora and its relatives

proposal.lay_description: Despite evidence that endophytes play a critical role in plant-microbe interactions they are poorly represented in genome databases. Leveraging our unique culture collection, we propose a genomic survey of the Xylariaceae, one of the largest and most diverse families of fungi made up of endophytic, pathogenic, and saprotrophic (including wood degrading) species. Our project will uncover the evolutionary history of plant-endophyte symbioses as well as characterize secondary metabolite (natural product) pathways and plant cell wall grading enzymes important for biofuel production in these fungi.
proposal.title: Comparative and population genomics of Xylariaceae: exploring the roles of endophytic fungi in lignocellulose degradation, nutrient cycling, and secondary metabolite production

proposal.lay_description: Genomes of important model and many industrially important fungi are still incomplete. The goal of this project is: (a) to finish and annotate the genomes of ~25 strains, and (b) to carry out functional analyses by novel CRISPR/Cas9 approaches. The next quantum leap in biology will come by integrating all levels of genome, transcriptome, proteome, and metabolome data for detailed cross-species comparisons. Completion of this CSP will have sweeping impact on data interpretation of current and completed genome-wide studies and will advance evolutionary and chromatin biology.
proposal.title: The curse of being first meets the need to be complete: Finishing genomes to leverage additional information from completed and ongoing JGI CSPs

proposal.lay_description: DNA methylation is a fundamental epigenetic modification that plays a critical role in genome function in eukaryotes This proposal will study the function of N6-methyladenine (6mA) in early divergent fungi because it is more abundant than in other eukaryotes and seems to regulate gene expression. The function will be studied in the context of responses to developmental and environmental signals, with special emphasis in those signals regulating lipid accumulation because of its relevancy for the production of biofuels.
proposal.title: Exploring the role of DNA methylation in biofuel production, environmental sensing and development in basal fungi

proposal.lay_description: Despite evidence that endophytes play a critical role in plant-microbe interactions they are poorly represented in genome databases. Leveraging our unique culture collection, we propose a genomic survey of the Xylariaceae, one of the largest and most diverse families of fungi made up of endophytic, pathogenic, and saprotrophic (including wood degrading) species. Our project will uncover the evolutionary history of plant-endophyte symbioses as well as characterize secondary metabolite (natural product) pathways and plant cell wall grading enzymes important for biofuel production in these fungi.
proposal.title: Comparative and population genomics of Xylariaceae: exploring the roles of endophytic fungi in lignocellulose degradation, nutrient cycling, and secondary metabolite production

Our proposal fits into the DOE mission because it focuses on biological processes of industrial interest, it explores the functional diversity of organisms that are essential for carbon cycling in ecosystems and it involves species related to N. crassa and P. anserina, model fungi for studying plant cell wall deconstruction.

proposal.lay_description: The species of yeasts that colonize floral nectar face two major challenges: high osmotic pressure caused by excessive carbon supply and strong resource competition caused by low nitrogen availability. This project is aimed at identifying the genes and pathways that enable nectar yeasts to grow in the carbon- and nitrogen-stressed environment. Nectar yeasts have presumably evolved strategies to scavenge nitrogen and continue biomass production under conditions where other microbes perish. Understanding the genomic basis of these strategies has the potential to facilitate redesigning of microbes for biofuel production and carbon storage.
proposal.title: Genomic basis of the ecological success of nectar yeasts in their carbon-stressed and nitrogen-limited environments

proposal.lay_description: Pine plantations in the Southern Hemisphere possess greatly impoverished assemblages of ectomycorrhizal fungi (EMF), often fewer than 20 species at a single forest site, compared to native populations of those same pines. The filtering results in a loss of some EMF lineages and may lead to large-scale impacts on soil biogeochemical processes. This work is to understand how co-introduction and subsequent co-invasion of pines and EMF into the Southern Hemisphere have driven the evolution of fungal genomes and genes required for EMF-plant communication and altered soil cycling in ecosystems.
proposal.title: Genetic, community, and ecosystem consequences of co-introduction of mycorrhizal fungi with exotic pines

proposal.lay_description: Trichoderma is a genus of fungi that has a broad impact on mankind. There are approximately 270 species of Trichoderma fungi that have varied interactions with other fungi, animals, plants, and efficiently degrade plant biomass material. One species in particular (T. reesei) is well-established for production of enzymes used in the biofuel and biorefinery industries. Trichoderma fungi promote plant growth by killing fungal pathogens or via production of chemicals that enhance growth or reduce plant stress.  To understand the biological and biochemical mechanisms underlying these characteristics and further enable new applications of these fungi and their products, we propose to determine and analyze the genetic blueprint of each of the 270 species of Trichoderma. The motivation for this project is the substantial impact that that the data would have on bio-energy, plant growth promotion and crop protection.
proposal.title: Genus-wide genomics of the biomass-degrading and plant-beneficial Trichoderma

One species in particular (T. reesei) is well-established for production of enzymes used in the biofuel and biorefinery industries. Trichoderma fungi promote plant growth by killing fungal pathogens or via production of chemicals that enhance growth or reduce plant stress.  To understand the biological and biochemical mechanisms underlying these characteristics and further enable new applications of these fungi and their products, we propose to determine and analyze the genetic blueprint of each of the 270 species of Trichoderma. The motivation for this project is the substantial impact that that the data would have on bio-energy, plant growth promotion and crop protection.

proposal.lay_description: Trichoderma is a genus of fungi that has a broad impact on mankind. There are approximately 270 species of Trichoderma fungi that have varied interactions with other fungi, animals, plants, and efficiently degrade plant biomass material. One species in particular (T. reesei) is well-established for production of enzymes used in the biofuel and biorefinery industries. Trichoderma fungi promote plant growth by killing fungal pathogens or via production of chemicals that enhance growth or reduce plant stress.  To understand the biological and biochemical mechanisms underlying these characteristics and further enable new applications of these fungi and their products, we propose to determine and analyze the genetic blueprint of each of the 270 species of Trichoderma. The motivation for this project is the substantial impact that that the data would have on bio-energy, plant growth promotion and crop protection.

There are approximately 270 species of Trichoderma fungi that have varied interactions with other fungi, animals, plants, and efficiently degrade plant biomass material. One species in particular (T. reesei) is well-established for production of enzymes used in the biofuel and biorefinery industries. Trichoderma fungi promote plant growth by killing fungal pathogens or via production of chemicals that enhance growth or reduce plant stress.  To understand the biological and biochemical mechanisms underlying these characteristics and further enable new applications of these fungi and their products, we propose to determine and analyze the genetic blueprint of each of the 270 species of Trichoderma. The motivation for this project is the substantial impact that that the data would have on bio-energy, plant growth promotion and crop protection.
proposal.title: Genus-wide genomics of the biomass-degrading and plant-beneficial Trichoderma

proposal.lay_description: We propose to investigate the genetic bases of fungal thermophily, biomass-degradation, and fungal-bacterial interactions in Sordariales, an order of biomass-degrading fungi frequently encountered in compost and encompassing one of the few groups of thermophilic fungi. Our proposal fits into the DOE mission because it focuses on biological processes of industrial interest, it explores the functional diversity of organisms that are essential for carbon cycling in ecosystems and it involves species related to N. crassa and P. anserina, model fungi for studying plant cell wall deconstruction.
proposal.title: Comparative genomics and association mapping in Sordariales: insights into functional diversity in Neurospora and its relatives

organisms.label: Genome

proposal.lay_description: Despite evidence that endophytes play a critical role in plant-microbe interactions they are poorly represented in genome databases. Leveraging our unique culture collection, we propose a genomic survey of the Xylariaceae, one of the largest and most diverse families of fungi made up of endophytic, pathogenic, and saprotrophic (including wood degrading) species. Our project will uncover the evolutionary history of plant-endophyte symbioses as well as characterize secondary metabolite (natural product) pathways and plant cell wall grading enzymes important for biofuel production in these fungi.
proposal.title: Comparative and population genomics of Xylariaceae: exploring the roles of endophytic fungi in lignocellulose degradation, nutrient cycling, and secondary metabolite production

Our project will uncover the evolutionary history of plant-endophyte symbioses as well as characterize secondary metabolite (natural product) pathways and plant cell wall grading enzymes important for biofuel production in these fungi.

proposal.lay_description: Despite evidence that endophytes play a critical role in plant-microbe interactions they are poorly represented in genome databases. Leveraging our unique culture collection, we propose a genomic survey of the Xylariaceae, one of the largest and most diverse families of fungi made up of endophytic, pathogenic, and saprotrophic (including wood degrading) species. Our project will uncover the evolutionary history of plant-endophyte symbioses as well as characterize secondary metabolite (natural product) pathways and plant cell wall grading enzymes important for biofuel production in these fungi.

proposal.lay_description: Despite evidence that endophytes play a critical role in plant-microbe interactions they are poorly represented in genome databases. Leveraging our unique culture collection, we propose a genomic survey of the Xylariaceae, one of the largest and most diverse families of fungi made up of endophytic, pathogenic, and saprotrophic (including wood degrading) species. Our project will uncover the evolutionary history of plant-endophyte symbioses as well as characterize secondary metabolite (natural product) pathways and plant cell wall grading enzymes important for biofuel production in these fungi.
